title: What’s Next in CX: 2026 Digital Customer Experience Trends
subtitle: Insights, strategies, and customer stories to plan and stay ahead
summary: This report outlines the top 5 digital experience trends for 2026 and provides tools, expert insights, and real-world case studies to help leaders act with confidence; it draws on a global survey of 1,692 CX leaders across roles and industries  . The trends are: 1) AI & automation, 2) Omnichannel experience, 3) Digital innovation, 4) Personalization, 5) Data-driven insights .

sections.title: Everything you need to know about the future of CX
The top 5 digital experience trends for 2026
The future of CX starts here and now

trends.name: AI & automation
trends.description: AI and automation dominate 2026, nearly 3x any other trend; momentum centers on automation, conversational agents, and generative AI .

subtrends.name: Automation
subtrends.note: Automation is the fastest path to scale, accelerating decision-making and surfacing insights for next best actions .

subtrends.name: Conversational agents
subtrends.note: Conversational AI handles routine tasks; it’s predicted 70% of customer interactions will begin and end with assistants by 2028 .

subtrends.name: Generative AI
subtrends.note: GenAI speeds creation of tailored content and knowledge assets, improving support quality and consistency .

trends.name: Omnichannel experience
trends.description: Climbs to second place as companies focus on better journeys across every channel and platform; connected data prevents breaks at handoffs .

subtrends.name: Connected journeys
subtrends.note: Analyze end-to-end journeys across platforms and channels to design seamless experiences .

subtrends.name: Touchpoint consistency
subtrends.note: Unify guidelines and ensure similar experiences across digital and physical channels to build trust and loyalty .

trends.name: Digital innovation
trends.description: Innovation focuses on agility and embedding AI into products; teams move from quick pilots to scaled features, enabled by modern tech stacks and ways of working .

subtrends.name: Faster piloting and productizing
subtrends.note: Scale successful AI-powered features quickly to win attention .

subtrends.name: Modern tech stacks
subtrends.note: Experience intelligence platforms unify data, automation, and collaboration; value requires evolving workflows too .

trends.name: Personalization
trends.description: Now a baseline powered by AI; analytics/data teams lead efforts to operationalize models at scale .

subtrends.name: Segmentation and targeting
subtrends.note: Backbone of personalization; groups customers by behaviors/preferences and sets up predictive models .

subtrends.name: Hyper-personalization
subtrends.note: Delivers relevance at scale by adapting in real time to context and intent .

trends.name: Data-driven insights
trends.description: Leaders prioritize actionable analytics, faster testing, and real-time data to move from analysis to execution .

subtrends.name: Actionable analytics
subtrends.note: Clean, unified, governed data turns insights into faster, smarter decisions .

subtrends.name: Real-time data
subtrends.note: Live behavioral signals power predictive CX and proactive interventions .

subtrends.name: Testing velocity
subtrends.note: Rapid experimentation boosts ROI by scaling winners and cutting losses quickly .

highlights: AI remains top, with new focus on automation .
Omnichannel experience rises to second, emphasizing connected journeys and touchpoint consistency .
Digital innovation enters top 5, reflecting AI-driven differentiation .
Personalization falls from second to fourth .
Data shifts to actionable insights and faster testing/decisions .

methodology: Based on 1,692 responses to Contentsquare’s global survey of digital professionals across marketing, UX, product, ecommerce, and technology; responses were cleaned (unified terms, translated) and grouped into 5 themes and 12 sub-trends to clarify priorities for 2026 .
about_publisher: Contentsquare is an all-in-one experience intelligence platform used to optimize experiences on 1.3M+ websites; its AI-powered insights help teams move faster and improve digital journeys
